plan.title: Child Fitness Improvement
plan.subtitle: Comparing baseline and endline metrics by location and coach

panels.title: Total Children
panels.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "Child ID") AS n FROM "baseline" UNION ALL SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "Child ID") AS n FROM "endline"

panels.title: Avg Height Change by Location
panels.sql: WITH diffs AS (SELECT "Location", AVG("Height cm") - ANY_VALUE("Height cm") OVER (PARTITION BY "Child ID") AS change FROM "baseline" b JOIN "endline" e ON b."Child ID" = e."Child ID"), SELECT "Location", SUM(change) AS diff FROM diffs GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10

panels.title: Avg Sit-ups Change by Coach
panels.sql: WITH diffs AS (SELECT "Coach", AVG("Sit ups") - ANY_VALUE("Sit ups") OVER (PARTITION BY "Child ID") AS change FROM "baseline" b JOIN "endline" e ON b."Child ID" = e."Child ID"), SELECT "Coach", SUM(change) AS diff FROM diffs GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10

panels.title: Avg Shuttle Run Change by Location
panels.sql: WITH diffs AS (SELECT "Location", AVG("Shuttle run sec") - ANY_VALUE("Shuttle run sec") OVER (PARTITION BY "Child ID") AS change FROM "baseline" b JOIN "endline" e ON b."Child ID" = e."Child ID"), SELECT "Location", SUM(change) AS diff FROM diffs GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 ASC LIMIT 10

panels.title: Top 10 Height Gainers
panels.sql: SELECT b."Child name", b."Location", b."Coach", (e."Height cm" - b."Height cm") AS gain FROM "baseline" b JOIN "endline" e ON b."Child ID" = e."Child ID" ORDER BY gain DESC LIMIT 10

panels.title: Top 10 Sit-ups Gainers
panels.sql: SELECT b."Child name", b."Location", b."Coach", (e."Sit ups" - b."Sit ups") AS gain FROM "baseline" b JOIN "endline" e ON b."Child ID" = e."Child ID" ORDER BY gain DESC LIMIT 10

plan.narrative: This dashboard tracks the physical progress of children from baseline to endline measurements. The first panel shows the total number of unique children recorded in the dataset. Subsequent bar charts break down the average improvement in height, sit-ups, and shuttle run times by location and coach, highlighting which groups saw the most significant gains. The tables list the individual children with the highest improvements in height and sit-ups, providing specific examples of success.
